source: Food Standards Agency Food Hygiene Rating Scheme (FHRS) open data, ratings.food.gov.uk

headlines.text: City of London Corporation has London's highest concentration of specialty coffee: 26 venues, 5.73x the London rate.
Haringey leads on bakeries and bagel shops: 1.9x the London rate.
City of London Corporation has the most wine, craft and cocktail bars for its size (3.14x London).
Lambeth is where plant-based places cluster (2.47x London).

CR4 looks like a scene that is still growing: 4.6 specialty, bakery, craft or plant-based places per 100 venues and 27.5% of venues awaiting a first inspection (new premises, new operators or backlog).
Emerging, lots of openings but the scene has not formed yet: NW9, IG3, IG1.
Established scenes with little new supply: N13, E17, N4.
City of London Corporation is the most chain-heavy borough, by the national chains we track (8.5% of venues) and Hackney the least (1.9%). London overall: 4.4%.
CR4 has the freshest supply: 27.5% of its 153 venues are awaiting a first inspection.
London's eating and drinking supply is slowing: 2.4 net new premises a day early in the window, -2.3 a day recently.

method: Keyword matches on premises names within eating and drinking premises, and share of premises awaiting their first FSA inspection. Proxies: a name can mislead, and awaiting inspection also covers changes of operator.
